title: Pepper Field Protocol 2018 - FFAR/Bee Better Survey
author: Lauren Ponisio
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rwtd7en
materials: Each person should have the following field supplies prepared: fanny pack for dry ice, 50 screw-top vials, spray bottle filled with ethanol, spray bottle filled with bleach + water (approx. 10% bleach), nitrile gloves (at least 5 pairs), Kestral with working batteries, stopwatch with working batteries, Ziploc bags for specimen storage, thin sharpie, weather data sheets, clean net Field lead should also have the following supplies: GPS with working batteries, Falcon tubes, transect tape, flagging tape/pin flags, dry shipper or dry ice cooler Net bags should be soaked in a solution of bleach and water for 5 minutes on any days off to ensure complete sterilization. Make sure to completely rinse net bags afterwards and allow to air-dry overnight. Net handles should also be wiped with the same bleach solution on days off as well.
Establish list of sites working with farm managers
Supplies : gloves, ethanol, bleach, sharpies, dry shipper/dry ice cooler, Ziplocs, screw-top tubes, weather data slips, Kestral, stopwatch, insect net
Supplies : gloves, ethanol, bleach, lighters, forceps, 15mL Falcon tubes, Ziplocs, sharpies, dry shipper/dry ice cooler

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Sterilize Nets
steps.instruction: Ensure all necessary equipment is gathered, including Kestral, stopwatch, GPS, transect tapes, and sterilization supplies. Maintain net cleanliness on off-days.

substeps.instruction: Soak net bags in a bleach and water solution for 5 minutes on days off, then rinse and air dry overnight.
Wipe net handles with the same bleach and water solution on days off.

steps.title: Establish Site and Transects
steps.instruction: Upon arrival at the site, locate or establish three 50m transects. Sampling must occur within 10m from the edge of each transect.

steps.title: Initial Sterilization
steps.instruction: Put on nitrile gloves and sterilize both gloves and forceps using bleach and ethanol.

steps.title: Collect No-Template Control (NTC)
steps.instruction: Collect a control sample into a vial and a separate control into a 25 ml falcon tube.

substeps.instruction: Label the vial with the date, site abbreviation, and the word 'control'; label the cap with site initials and 'C'.
Hold the vial open to the air for 30 seconds, then close it.
Place the vial back inside the Ziploc bag.

steps.title: Measure Environmental Conditions
steps.instruction: Use the Kestral to measure temperature and windspeed to determine if sampling can proceed.

substeps.instruction: Temperature: Stand in a sunny spot, hold the Kestral away from the body, and shade the white monitor. Ensure units are in Celsius. Wait for stabilization. Collection is only permitted between 17C and 24C.
Wind: Stand facing the wind with the Kestral perpendicular so the propeller spins. Use the average windspeed screen (AVG) in m/s. Wait for stabilization. Collection is only permitted below 2.5 m/s.
Record the stable temperature, average windspeed, and the time of collection.

steps.title: Configure Sampling Stopwatch
steps.instruction: Set the stopwatch to countdown mode for 30-minute active sampling increments.

substeps.instruction: Toggle to countdown mode using the center (mode) button.
Reset to 30'00'00 using the left (split/reset) button; if necessary, hold left and center buttons to reset to 0, then use the left button to toggle and right button to set MM to 30.
Exit edit mode with the center button.

steps.title: Collect Wild Bees and Insects
steps.instruction: Search transects for wild bees (including honey bees), flies, or wasps visiting flowers for a total of 3 active sampling hours per transect (9 hours per site).

substeps.instruction: Start the stopwatch when active sampling begins.
Stop the stopwatch immediately upon catching an insect.
While the timer is stopped, place the insect in a vial and sterilize gloves.
Restart the timer when returning to active sampling.

Label each vial with: Site code, Transect number, Bee type (if known), Plant collected from, Date, and Collector initials (e.g., WS2-HR, Anthophora, Purple Sage, 2/12/18, KCT). Label the top of the vial with site initials.
Avoid talking during collection and aim the vial away from the mouth.

steps.title: Post-Sampling Weather Recording
steps.instruction: Once the 30 minutes of active sampling are completed, record the weather and windspeed again using the Kestral.

steps.title: Collect Flower Samples
steps.instruction: Collect flower samples from each of the three transects.

substeps.instruction: Randomly select 5 plants per transect.
Collect 1 flower from each plant (including petals, stamen, stigma, etc.) and place all 5 flowers from one transect into a single vial.
Avoid damaging the flower; if too many petals fall outside the tube, replace the flower.
Label vials with: Site, Transect, Flowers + Round Number, Date, and Collector Initials (e.g., HC3, Flowers Round 2, 3/1/18, KCT).
Fully sterilize gloves and forceps between trees using bleach and ethanol; flame sterilize forceps once ethanol has dried.

steps.title: Store and Transport Samples
steps.instruction: Secure all collected samples in Ziploc bags and place them in the dry shipper.

substeps.instruction: Place all wild bee samples from all collectors into a Ziploc labeled with site, date, and 'wild bee'.
Place all three transects' flower tubes into a single Ziploc labeled with site, date, and 'Flowers Round #'.

steps.title: Maintain Glove Sterilization
steps.instruction: Wear fitting nitrile gloves throughout field and lab work. Change gloves often.

substeps.instruction: To sterilize: Thoroughly wet gloves with bleach, rub hands together, and air dry. Then, thoroughly wet with ethanol and air dry.
Avoid touching face, clothes, or skin after sterilization.

steps.title: Handle Vials Aseptically
steps.instruction: Prevent contamination of vials during preparation and use.

substeps.instruction: When opening bags of vials, pour them onto a cleaned, sterilized surface (e.g., UV hood or sterilized tray) rather than reaching inside the bag.
Do not touch the inside of vials or breathe into them.
